justification: Names the exact root-causing lines (the fillPendingConnectQueue/consumeConnectionBacklog body, 355-362) and states both required conditions: the non-blocking connect loop returns before the handshakes have saturated the backlog-1 accept queue, and the connect-deadline check's catch (SocketTimeoutException) -> assertExceptionContains("...: connect timed out") then sees a read deadline. It also derives the correct discriminator (only the tests that call the helper fail). This is the defect the upstream fix repairs by waiting for a probe connect to time out.
claimed_lines: TestWebHdfsClientDeadlines.java:355-362 fillPendingConnectQueue() — the non-blocking connect loop
TestWebHdfsClientDeadlines.java:155-156 and :185-186 assertExceptionContains("...: connect timed out")
claimed_branches: configureBlocking(false) + connect() only initiate the SYN; finishConnect() is never called, so on return from fillPendingConnectQueue there is no guarantee the kernel accept queue is full

if the client's SYN arrives while the accept queue still has room the handshake completes and the 200 ms read timeout fires instead of the connect timeout; the catch/assertExceptionContains for ": connect timed out" then fails
the read-deadline tests do not call fillPendingConnectQueue and therefore cannot regress this way
gt_lines: TestWebHdfsTimeouts.consumeConnectionBacklog() body, pre-fix lines 355-362 (anonymized: TestWebHdfsClientDeadlines.fillPendingConnectQueue()) — the non-blocking SocketChannel connect loop that returns without confirming the accept queue is saturated; the fix appends a GenericTestUtils.waitFor probe (blocking connect with a 100 ms deadline, polling 100 ms up to 10 s) plus the failedToConsumeBacklog field / assumeBacklogConsumed()
the assumeBacklogConsumed() calls added inside the catch (SocketTimeoutException) blocks of testRedirectConnectTimeout (pre-fix line 216) and testTwoStepWriteConnectTimeout (pre-fix line 249)
gt_branches: the loop's only exit condition is the fixed count i < CLIENTS_TO_CONSUME_BACKLOG (129), not the state it stands for; combined with client.configureBlocking(false) the connect() calls only initiate handshakes, so the accept queue of new ServerSocket(0, CONNECTION_BACKLOG=1) can still have room when the helper returns

the connect-deadline checks then take the wrong arm: catch (SocketTimeoutException e) -> GenericTestUtils.assertExceptionContains(authority + ": connect timed out", e) receives a ": Read timed out" exception (or no exception at all -> fail("expected timeout"))
